source: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-25 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-25.pdf), the section 36B(b)(3)(A) applicable percentage table for taxable years beginning in 2026, and the ARPA/IRA enhanced table (Public Law 117-2 section 9661, extended by Public Law 117-169 section 12001) that applied 2021 through 2025.
confidenceNote: The 2026 table was checked 2026-10-01 against the Finance Buff, nationaltaxtools and Current Federal Tax Developments transcriptions of Rev. Proc. 2025-25 (irs.gov unreachable from the build session). Status of the enhanced credits checked the same day: they expired 31 December 2025 and no extension had been enacted (KFF, CNBC 6 January 2026, CRS R48290), so the cliff rule is current law.
note: Read by engine/tax/aca.js (D-341). Expected contribution = applicable percentage times MAGI, where the percentage is interpolated linearly inside each band of MAGI as a share of the federal poverty line. Under the cliff rule there is no credit above 400% FPL (and none below 100% FPL, where Medicaid or nothing applies). Under the enhanced rule the contribution is capped at the top percentage with no ceiling. The engine's default follows `currentLaw`.

cliff.label: Current law for 2026: credit ends at 400% of the poverty line

enhanced.label: The 2021 to 2025 enhanced table, no cliff, if Congress restores it
